_meta.keys: Key n: ML-DSA-65 seed [n]*32, Ed25519 seed [n+100]*32. Holders A,B,C,D = 1,2,3,4; seats 11,12; witnesses 21,22,23; stranger 9; A's other key 31; C's rotated key 33; recovery key of holder n = n+50; A's signing key after its first recovery 41, after its second 42; A's next recovery keys 61, 62; a key no commitment names 71.
_meta.spec: CC 2.6.1.11 / 4.2.6 / 4.2.2.1 / 3.3.6.1 / 3.3.6.2 / 3.2 T3 / 5.3.4, CIRISConstitution v1.0-rc21 b016df4; dial_hints as proposed for rc22
_meta.verdicts: valid | invalid (token genesis_bundle_malformed, detail = reason) | waiting {rows, prev, kids} | nothing (token; detail = the row, custody or commitment fault)

cases.description: The first bundle: three holders, two seats, every holder signed, thumbprint anchor.
The same bundle under its object id as the anchor.
The valid bundle and a fourth statement by a key in no role: refused, the rest stand.
Witnessed mode on: three witnesses, quorum 2, each witness's record cited.
Two of three holders signed a first bundle: the count is unmet.
C's statement carries iat one second late: that statement is refused (iat_mismatch); the count is unmet. CC's reference reader answers Invalid iat_mismatch for the bundle.
C's statement carries no sub: refused on its own (statement_sub_not_family); the count is unmet.
C's statement names another lineage as its sub: refused on its own.
C's statement carries no iat: refused before grouping; the count is unmet.
C's signature has one byte flipped: refused; the count is unmet.
A's statement names A's iss but is signed under another key: refused in a first bundle.
A row statement offered as a bundle voice: refused; the count is unmet.
A statement of typ ceg-revocation-snapshot/2 over the same payload: refused.
A holder set unlike the thumbprint anchor: not anchored.
An object id unlike the anchor: not anchored.
A reader with no anchor promotes nothing to a root.
Seat 1's key record is named but not held: Waiting on it.
A row held under another id than the one named: the named row is not held.
Seat 2's binding is not in cites: a seat with no binding, unplaced.
A stranger's key record named in cites: a row with no place.
Two key records by holder A: two rows for one place.
Seat 1's key record with a flipped signature byte (same row id): Invalid as a row.
Seat 1's record is node + pseudonym, not exactly node.
Seat 1's node record has no valid_until: key_record_out_of_window.
Holder B's record carries user, not accord_holder.
Holder A's record (author A) records another key: not A's genesis key.
Holder A's record signed by B's key: not signed by the key it records.
Seat 1's record ends at the bundle's own asserted_at: it does not cover the bundle's instant (valid_until must be later).
Seat 1's record ended a day before the bundle.
CC sample: a pq_custody outside the three (token): the record is refused.
CC sample: a chain in hex (text, not bytes): the record is refused.
CC sample: an empty chain: the record is refused.
Holder A's ML-DSA half software_wrapped: fails the gate.
Holder B's chain verifies only to a root the reader does not trust.
Holder C's chain attests an Ed25519 key that is not its record's half.
Holder A's f9 certificate carries no FIPS extension: the floor is not met.
Holder A asserts YubiKey_5_FIPS with no chain: unattested, not seated.
Holder A's record carries no attestation_evidence: no class, not seated.
Seat 1's binding (author S1) signed by seat 2's key.
transit_xwing_pubkey of 1215 bytes.
No onion_hop_xwing_pubkey.
The onion key's X25519 half equals the transit key's.
The transit key's X25519 half is the RNS link x25519.
The onion key's X25519 half is the seat's own Ed25519 half.
The binding also carries the earlier transit_kex_pubkeys pair.
The seat carries onion_relay.opt_out: seat_opted_out.
An identity:occurrence by the seat with no transport_destination.
Seat 1's binding carries no refs: it names no key record (CC 3.3.6.2).
Seat 1's binding names seat 2's key record, not its own.
CC sample: an X-Wing key inside transport_destination, a closed map of the five RNS members: the binding is Invalid as a row.
CC sample: destination_hash as hex text, not 16 bytes.
CC sample: onion_relay {opt_out: false}; the member is only ever {opt_out: true}.
Seat 1's binding with no identity_key_id: off the identity:occurrence rule.
Seat 1's binding whose refs name no self-roster head (CC 3.3.6.4): off the identity:occurrence rule.
Seat 1's binding with no occurrence_key_id: off the identity:occurrence rule.
Seat 1's binding of device_class laptop (in the closed set, not server).
CC's reader sample: seat 1's binding of device_class phone.
Seat 1's binding of device_class tablet, outside the closed set.
Seat 1's binding with no device_class.
Seat 1's binding whose identity_key_id names seat 2: not the seat's identity reference.
Seat 1's binding whose occurrence_key_id names seat 2.
Seat 1's binding whose identity_key_id is a bare key label, not an identity reference.
Seat 1's binding (author, identity_key_id and occurrence_key_id S1) under CWT sub S2: occurrence_key_id is not the sub. CC's reader projection carries no sub, so it is not modelled.
Seat 1's binding carries no dial_hints: a fresh node cannot dial it.
Seat 1's binding carries udp and http hints but no tcp hint.
Seat 1's binding carries only an unknown hint type: skipped, so no tcp.
Seat 1's tcp hint has port 0: a known type with a bad body.
Seat 1's tcp hint host carries a space.
Seat 1's http hint is not https (beside a good tcp hint).
Seat 1's rnode hint body is 9 bytes, not 10.
Seat 1's dial_hints is an empty array (absence is the one encoding of none).
Seat 1's dial_hints carries five entries (the bound is 4).
Seat 1's dial_hints entry is [1], not [type, body].
Seat 1's dial_hints entry body is text, not bytes.
Seat 1's dial_hints entry type is 256.
version 2 with no prev.
version 1 with a prev.
A holder also listed in serve_nodes.
A seat also listed as a witness.
Commitments keyed by two of the three holders.
scope without infra:attest.
witnesses and witness_quorum without witness_cadence_secs.
Three witnesses with quorum 3 (floor(3/2)+1 is 2).
holders not in CDE order.
scope as [infra:attest, infra:serve], not in CDE set order (the shorter text first).
A cites row-ref of edition 1.
halt_fuse_secs 0.
Version 2: C swapped for D; a strict majority of the predecessor's holders (A, B) and D sign.
A and the removed holder C (under its key from the predecessor) are the majority; D, the added holder, signs.
A and B sign but D, the added holder, does not: the count is unmet.
A and D only: one of three predecessor holders is no majority.

C signs under a key C rotated to, not the key the predecessor seats for C: that statement is refused (each later statement is under the key the predecessor names), and A alone of the predecessor's holders is no majority. v1 answered Waiting on the key.
The predecessor is not held: Waiting on it.
The predecessor is held and not Valid: the bundle concludes nothing.
Version 3 naming a version-1 predecessor.
A later bundle with another family_key_id.
B's recovery commitment changes but B does not sign (A and C do).
B's recovery commitment changes and B signs, with A.
A and the stranger X sign: X has no role, A alone is no majority.

A recovers: one statement by A's recovery key (iss A, kid the recovery key, its record named), A's new signing-key record named, A's commitment the next one. It counts on that statement alone; A's first commitment is spent.
A recovery under a key whose record is named but which A's commitment in force does not commit to: the statement does not count.
A's lone statement under A's current signing key, with its record and A's new record named: that key is not the one A's commitment commits to.
A recovery whose recovery key's record is not named: the key does not resolve, and the statement does not count.
A recovery whose next commitment is the one it spends.
A recovery whose new signing-key record holds the recovery key itself.
A recovery seating as A's signing key B's recovery key, a key a commitment of the lineage commits to.
A recovery naming A's current record as the new one: the new key is A's current key.
A recovery that also re-commits B.
A recovery that also changes halt_fuse_secs.
A recovery that also drops seat 2.
The recovery statement's signature has a byte flipped: refused; nothing counts.
A recovers again, under the recovery key its first recovery committed; both commitments it used are spent.
A second recovery under A's first recovery key, already spent.
A second recovery whose next commitment is the one the first spent.
A roster bundle (A under its new key, and B) setting A's commitment back to the one A's recovery spent: a spent commitment never returns.
After A's recovery, a roster bundle re-committing B, signed by A under its new key and B: A's record is the new one, which the bundle in force seats (not A's genesis key), and passes.

After A's recovery, a roster bundle B and C sign naming A's genesis record, a key the recovery retired: holder_key_retired (Invalid, read from the payload and the predecessor; it answers before holder_not_genesis_key, which turns on the statements held).
Without a recovery, a roster bundle every holder signs, A under its current (genesis) key, naming a new record for A: A's own counted statement re-seats A at the new key.
The same bundle counted on B and C alone: A's statement is not among the counted, so A's new record is not the key the bundle in force seats for A.

The same bundle with A's statement under the new key: refused (statement_kid_not_iss, not the key the predecessor seats); B and C meet the count, but A's statement under its current key is not among the counted, so A's new record is holder_not_genesis_key.
The next bundle after A's rotation re-commits B, signed by A under its new key (the one the predecessor now seats) and B: Valid.
After A rotated to a new key, a roster bundle A (under its new key) and B sign re-seating A at its genesis key, which the lineage retired: holder_key_retired.
After A's recovery, a roster bundle A (under its recovered key), B and C sign re-seating A at its genesis key, which the recovery retired: holder_key_retired.
A roster bundle every holder signs (A under its current key) seating A at the key A's recovery commitment in force commits to: holder_key_retired.
After A's recovery, a roster bundle A (under its recovered key), B and C sign seating A at the recovery key that recovery spent: holder_key_retired.
Two first bundles every anchored holder signed: both Valid, a fork of the genesis.
The same two first bundles under an object-id anchor: the other is void.
Two Valid version-2 bundles naming one prev: a fork.
The valid version-2 bundle over its predecessor: the head is version 2.

Two later bundles count on one predecessor: C swapped for D (A, B, D sign), and A's recovery. A fork: the reader holds both as tips and acts on what both name, B and the two seats (A's key differs between the tips; C and D stand in one each).
